clue.text: Transgressed concerning a plain before a large number

indicators.note: the plain is placed in front of the number in the answer

parts.note: over can mean about or concerning, as in a row over money
a steppe is a vast treeless plain
D is the Roman numeral for 500, a large number

explanation.surface: Someone went too far by heading for a prairie ahead of a big crowd.
explanation.definitionFit: To go beyond a permitted limit is to transgress it, the literal image being a stride past a line.

clue.text: Instrument for one in a little book

indicators.note: the single letter sits inside the abbreviation for a book

parts.note: VOL is the short form of volume, a book cut down
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A music lover asks for an instrument in exchange for a slim volume.
explanation.definitionFit: A viol is a bowed stringed instrument of the Renaissance, ancestor of the viola da gamba family.

clue.text: Artists seen on the page have a discordant effect

indicators.note: in a down clue one piece sitting on another stands above it

parts.note: RA stands for Royal Academician, so RAS are artists

explanation.surface: Painters featured in print strike a jarring note.
explanation.definitionFit: A harsh grating sound jars on the ear, so to rasp is to grate discordantly.

clue.text: Language used to draw the upper class after half-term

indicators.note: the pull and the class letter come after the half word
half of the four-letter word term is its first two letters

parts.note: to lug something is to drag or draw it along
U is the old label for upper-class usage, as in U and non-U

explanation.surface: Some school language is used to lure posh pupils once the half-term holiday is over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'half-term' looks like a school holiday, but it only supplies the opening pair of 'term'. Telugu is a Dravidian language of south-east India.
explanation.definitionFit: Telugu is a major Dravidian tongue spoken in Andhra Pradesh, one of India's official languages.

clue.text: Methods of selling property that is in entertainment which is not public

parts.note: something private is not open to the public

indicators.note: the abbreviation for that is goes inside the word for entertainments

parts.note: treats are pleasures laid on to entertain someone
IE is the abbreviation of id est, Latin for that is

explanation.surface: An estate agent explains the property sale held as a private party, not open to the public.
explanation.walkthrough: A private treaty sale is the British term for selling a house by direct negotiation rather than at auction.
explanation.definitionFit: A private treaty is a sale of property agreed directly between parties rather than by auction.

clue.text: Concerning banishment of a team in the end of survival

indicators.note: the team's numerals are put inside the shortened word for a survival
only the end part of the word is kept, its head letter falling away

parts.note: a relic is something surviving from the past, a survival
XI is eleven in Roman numerals, a cricket or football team

explanation.surface: A question about exile asks whether a side can last to the end of the competition.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the end of' keeps the tail of the word for a survival, dropping its first letter. Exilic refers to the Jewish exile in Babylon.
explanation.definitionFit: Exilic describes things belonging to a period of exile, especially the Babylonian captivity of the Jews.

clue.text: Instances of self-pollination turn up among unusual city males

indicators.note: the reversed word is placed in the middle of the scrambled letters
unusual tells us the letters of city males appear in a strange order
in a down clue up means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: a go is a turn, as in a game

explanation.surface: A botanist notes curious urban men taking their turn.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unusual' rearranges the letters of 'city males', and the reversed turn word sits among them. The printed 'self-pollution' should read self-pollination.
explanation.definitionFit: Cleistogamy is pollination within flowers that never open, so the plant fertilises itself.

clue.text: Kind of record for performance in desire

indicators.note: the performance goes inside the word for desire

parts.note: longing is a strong desire
a play is a theatrical performance

explanation.surface: A show business type asks for a recording that satisfies the urge to perform.
explanation.walkthrough: 'performance' first suggests a record's quality, but it is the piece placed in the middle of the desire word.
explanation.definitionFit: The long-playing record, or LP, is a vinyl disc turning at 33 rpm that holds an album.

clue.text: Voice to get her in unison

definitions.text: Voice to get her in unison

parts.words: Voice to get her in unison
parts.note: the singing part followed by the words to get her runs on into the word for in unison, all together

explanation.surface: A choirmaster wants a part sung so the singers come in together.
explanation.walkthrough: Write the voice part and add 'to get her': the two overlap into ALTOGETHER, which means in unison. The voice is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Alto is the lower female or high male singing part in a choir.

clue.text: Illness which makes one rest back on a heavy bed

indicators.note: the last two pieces come after the first two in the answer

parts.note: a ton is a heavyweight, so heavy gives the weight word
a sill is a flat bed of rock lying between other strata
I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: back means the word for resting is read in reverse

parts.note: to sit is to rest in a seat

explanation.surface: An ailment forces a patient to lie down on a hefty bed.
explanation.walkthrough: A sill in geology is a flat sheet of rock lying between beds, which is how 'bed' gets its piece.
explanation.definitionFit: Tonsillitis is the inflammation of the tonsils, a common throat infection.

clue.text: Phone and get the engaged signal?

explanation.surface: Someone calls a number and hears the busy tone.
explanation.walkthrough: The engaged signal is not the busy tone on a phone line but the token worn by a person engaged to marry.
explanation.definitionFit: To phone someone is to ring them, and a fiancée's engagement ring announces the betrothal.

clue.text: Town in which one fruit appears beneath the water

indicators.note: in a down clue the later pieces are written underneath the water

parts.note: a pond is a small body of water
I is the Roman numeral for one
a cherry is a small stone fruit

explanation.surface: In some town a single piece of fruit is found under the surface of a lake.
explanation.definitionFit: Pondicherry, now Puducherry, is a former French colonial town on India's south-east coast.

clue.text: Effeminate males acted differently about the beginning of union

indicators.note: the scrambled letters go round the opening letter of union
the letters of males acted are set out in a different order
the beginning of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: Unmanly men behaved oddly when trade unions first came into the picture.
explanation.walkthrough: 'differently' rearranges MALES ACTED to EMASCLATED around U, the first letter of 'union', making EMASCULATED.
explanation.definitionFit: To be emasculated is to be deprived of masculine vigour, so weakened and unmanly.

clue.text: A dynasty back in charge on the male side

indicators.note: back tells us the dynasty's name is written in reverse

parts.note: the Tang were a Chinese imperial dynasty

explanation.surface: A ruling family returns to power through the male line.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns TANG to GNAT.
explanation.definitionFit: Agnatic kinship is traced through male ancestors only, the father's line.

clue.text: Asserted the old just about measure up

indicators.note: the elderly word goes around the reversed measure

parts.note: the aged are old people

indicators.note: in a down clue up means read from the bottom

parts.note: an ell is an old cloth measure of about 45 inches

explanation.surface: Older people claimed they could just about measure up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'just' is padding linking the two halves. An ell is an old cloth measure.
explanation.definitionFit: Something alleged has been claimed or declared, without yet being proved.

clue.text: Clap his being employed by rulers

indicators.note: being put to work, the letters of clap his are set to a new use

explanation.surface: Someone is hired to applaud the monarchs.
explanation.definitionFit: Caliphs were the successors of Muhammad who ruled the Islamic world.

clue.text: Means of decoration which necessitates rearranging a room with half the attraction

indicators.note: rearranging asks for the letters of room in a new order
only half of the word for attraction is kept, the first two letters

parts.note: a lure is an attraction or enticement

explanation.surface: A decorator rearranges a room to make it half as appealing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rearranging' turns ROOM into ORMO; 'half' cuts LURE to LU.
explanation.definitionFit: Ormolu is gilded bronze used to ornament furniture and clocks.

clue.text: Ring for what is left on the bill

indicators.note: the letter for left is added onto the end of the menu word

parts.note: the carte is a bill of fare, a menu

explanation.surface: Someone asks for a call about the remainder still on the bill.
explanation.definitionFit: A ring is a group working to fix prices, and a cartel is such a price-fixing combination of firms.

clue.text: A woman on her own is about to encourage sadly

parts.note: Di is a short woman's name

indicators.note: the word for alone goes around the word for encourage

parts.note: singly means one by one, on one's own
to hearten is to encourage

explanation.surface: A lonely woman is ready to give herself some cheer in her sorrow.
explanation.walkthrough: Di is short for Diana; 'is' links the pieces. 'sadly' looks like an anagram signal but is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Something done dishearteningly dampens spirits, in a manner that leaves one sad.

clue.text: Rotter about to avail himself of what has been produced

indicators.note: the scoundrel goes around the word for using

parts.note: a cad is a dishonourable man, a rotter
to avail oneself of something is to use it

explanation.surface: A scoundrel sets out to exploit what others have made.
explanation.walkthrough: Rotter and cad are dated British words for a man who behaves badly.
explanation.definitionFit: To bring an effect about is to produce it, so caused works as a synonym of brought about.

clue.text: Lots turn up in the party machine

indicators.note: the reversed word for lots goes inside the party

parts.note: a do is a party or social event

indicators.note: in a down clue turn up means read the word from bottom to top

parts.note: many means a lot of

explanation.surface: Crowds arrive at the political party's election apparatus.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'turn up' reads the word from bottom to top, and 'party' is the social kind, not a political one.
explanation.definitionFit: A dynamo is an electrical generator, a machine turning motion into current.

clue.text: In silence a person acts as a magician

definitions.note: the description stands for the noun, one who acts as a magician

parts.note: sh is the call for silence
a man is a person

explanation.surface: A performer works quiet tricks.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition describes the person rather than naming them: a shaman acts as a magician for a tribe.
explanation.definitionFit: A shaman is a tribal priest believed to work magic and contact the spirit world.

clue.text: Possibly get sad when it is put on

indicators.note: possibly says the letters of get sad could be rearranged into another word

explanation.surface: Someone may become gloomy when it is time to perform.
explanation.definitionFit: A play is staged when it is mounted and performed, so put on in the theatre sense.

clue.text: Hardy subjects for rulers

explanation.surface: Thomas Hardy is asked to write about kings.
explanation.walkthrough: Thomas Hardy wrote The Dynasts, an epic drama about the Napoleonic Wars, so its title names his subjects.
explanation.definitionFit: Dynasts are hereditary rulers, and Hardy took them as the title figures of his verse drama.

clue.text: Man is backward in the old country

indicators.note: the word for a man is written in reverse order

parts.note: a male is a man

explanation.surface: A fellow is a little behind the times in the old country.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is backward' reverses MALE.
explanation.definitionFit: Elam was an ancient kingdom east of Babylonia, in what is now south-western Iran.

clue.text: In a point just above a sailor there is a heavenly body

indicators.note: in a down clue the compass letter is written directly over the sailor

parts.note: S, for south, is a point of the compass
a tar is a sailor, as in Jack Tar

explanation.surface: A celestial object seen at a spot just over a seaman's head.
explanation.definitionFit: A star is a luminous celestial body such as the Sun.

clue.text: Hoax right out of the fringe

indicators.note: the letter for right is taken out of the word for fringe

parts.note: a skirt is an edge or border, as in the outskirts

explanation.surface: A trick is played by someone excluded from the fringe festival.
explanation.definitionFit: A skit was once a jest or hoax at someone's expense; now it is a short comic sketch.

clue.text: One town having its foundations in front of another

indicators.note: the first piece is placed ahead of the second

parts.note: basing means putting on foundations
another town: Stoke, in the English Midlands

explanation.surface: One town is built on the base of another.
explanation.walkthrough: Basingstoke is a town in Hampshire; Stoke-on-Trent, often just Stoke, is a city in Staffordshire.
explanation.definitionFit: Basingstoke is a large market town in Hampshire in southern England.

clue.text: Welsh name for one who envisages the future being backwards

indicators.note: being backwards tells us the word for a prophet is written in reverse

parts.note: a seer is a prophet who foresees events

explanation.surface: A Welsh prophet has a name that looks behind rather than ahead.
explanation.definitionFit: Rees is a common Welsh surname, from the given name Rhys.

clue.text: Thoughtful when one is in a legal position inside the box

indicators.note: the legal position goes inside the box

parts.note: a crate is a wooden box
in football and rugby onside is the legal position on the pitch

explanation.surface: A kindly footballer stays legal inside the penalty box.
explanation.walkthrough: Onside is the opposite of offside in football, so it is the legal position; 'when one is in' links.
explanation.definitionFit: Considerate people are thoughtful of others' feelings.
